[name]
Baltimore, MD · [email] · [phone] · [url]

ACADEMIC APPOINTMENTS
Johns Hopkins University, Whiting School of Engineering — Baltimore, MD
Associate Professor (with tenure), Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, July 2023 – Present
Assistant Professor, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, July 2017 – June 2023
Secondary appointment, Department of Computer Science, 2020 – Present
Affiliated faculty, Mathematical Institute for Data Science and the Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics

EDUCATION
Ph.D., Electrical Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, 2015
Dissertation on sparse signal recovery for coherent imaging systems; Beckman Institute graduate fellow
M.S., Electrical Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, 2012
B.S., Electrical and Computer Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology, 2010, highest honors

POSTDOCTORAL TRAINING
Postdoctoral Research Associate, Department of Statistics, Columbia University, 2015 – 2017

RESEARCH
Computational imaging and statistical signal processing: inverse problems with learned priors, sparse and low-rank recovery, uncertainty quantification for medical and scientific imaging. The group currently has 7 Ph.D. students, 2 postdoctoral fellows and 4 undergraduate researchers.

HONORS AND AWARDS
- NSF CAREER Award, 2019
- Best Paper Award, IEEE International Conference on Computational Photography, 2021
- IEEE Signal Processing Society Early Career Technical Achievement Award, 2024
- Johns Hopkins Catalyst Award, 2019
- Whiting School of Engineering Excellence in Teaching Award, 2022
- Senior Member, IEEE, 2021
- Finalist, Young Author Best Paper Award, IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2017 (as doctoral author)

RESEARCH FUNDING (as principal investigator unless noted)
- NSF CAREER: learned priors for scientific imaging, 2019 – 2024, $548,000
- NIH R01 (co-PI with a radiology faculty member): uncertainty-aware reconstruction for low-dose CT, 2022 – 2027, $2.6M (PI share $1.3M)
- DARPA seedling: compressive imaging for low-light sensing, 2020 – 2022, $740,000
- NSF CCF Medium (lead PI, 3 institutions): algorithmic foundations of self-supervised inverse problems, 2023 – 2027, $1.2M (JHU share $650,000)
- Industry gifts and awards (two imaging companies, one cloud provider): $410,000 total since 2018
Total external funding as PI or co-PI: about $5.5M; as PI: about $3.4M

PUBLICATIONS
50 peer-reviewed publications (22 journal, 28 conference); 15 at top venues (IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ICLR); h-index 30; about 4,200 citations as of September 2026.

Selected (student authors from my group in positions 1 – 2 on most):
1. IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2025 — last author — self-supervised reconstruction with calibrated uncertainty
2. NeurIPS 2024 — last author — plug-and-play priors with convergence guarantees under model mismatch
3. CVPR 2024 — last author — joint denoising and super-resolution for low-light scientific cameras
4. SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences, 2023 — last author — provable recovery with learned proximal operators
5. ICML 2023 — second author (collaborator's student first) — diffusion priors for linear inverse problems
6. IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, 2022 — last author — unrolled networks for coherent imaging
7. IEEE ICCP 2021 — last author — single-shot compressive hyperspectral imaging (Best Paper Award)
8. ICLR 2021 — last author — equivariant imaging without ground truth
9. IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2019 — sole author — sharp phase-transition bounds for structured sparse recovery
10. IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2016 — first author — sparse recovery for coherent imaging (from the dissertation)

STUDENTS SUPERVISED
- 8 Ph.D. graduates (2021 – 2026): 3 now in faculty positions (two R1 universities, one liberal-arts college), 4 in industry research (imaging, semiconductor, cloud), 1 postdoctoral fellow
- 3 former postdoctoral fellows, all now in tenure-track positions
- 7 current Ph.D. students, 2 current postdoctoral fellows
- Supervised 19 undergraduate researchers; 6 are coauthors on published papers

TEACHING
- Developed and teach the graduate course Computational Imaging (enrollment about 45) and the undergraduate course Signals and Systems (enrollment about 120)
- Co-developed the department's first-year design course module on imaging sensors, 2021
- Mean teaching evaluation 4.6 / 5 across 14 course offerings
- Lecturer, IEEE Signal Processing Society summer school on computational imaging, 2023 and 2025

PROFESSIONAL SERVICE
- Associate Editor, IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging, 2022 – Present
- Area Chair: NeurIPS 2023, 2024, 2025; ICML 2024, 2025; CVPR 2025
- Technical Program Committee: IEEE ICCP (2020 – 2025), ICASSP (2018 – 2024)
- General Co-Chair, IEEE International Conference on Computational Photography, 2026
- NSF review panels (CCF, ECCS): 6 panels since 2018
- Member, IEEE Signal Processing Society Computational Imaging Technical Committee, 2020 – Present

INVITED TALKS (selected, 2023 – 2026)
Stanford Electrical Engineering seminar (2026); MIT Computational Imaging seminar (2025); Caltech IST seminar (2025); SIAM Conference on Imaging Science plenary-track minisymposium (2024); EPFL Center for Imaging (2024); Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (2023); 24 invited talks since 2018.

UNIVERSITY SERVICE
- Director of Graduate Admissions, ECE, 2022 – 2025 (about 900 applications a year)
- Faculty search committee chair, ECE, 2024 – 2025
- Whiting School diversity and climate committee, 2019 – 2022

PATENTS
- Three granted US patents on compressive and computational imaging systems (2019, 2022, 2024), licensed to one imaging-sensor company

PROFESSIONAL MEMBERSHIPS
IEEE (Senior Member), SIAM, Optica
